contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: benchmark scores overstate robust, general ability. The 2024 to post-date window is reasonable. The claim is partly conceptual, but the factual core can be checked.

evidence.note: ICLR 2025 GSM-Symbolic study, posted October 2024, before the post. Scores fall when only the numbers change or an irrelevant clause is added, which shows benchmark scores overstating reasoning.
Leaderboard Illusion preprint, April 2025, before the post. It finds Arena gains reflecting overfitting rather than general model quality.

reviews.rationale: Two credible studies from before the post show benchmark scores overstating general ability: performance drops under small changes, and rankings reflect overfitting. The packet has no counterevidence that benchmarks reliably track general capability. Under the plain reading, the claim holds.

attribution.note: Marcus co-wrote the post. The sentence is the authors' own judgment. Tao is invoked in the next sentence, which is a separate claim.

semantics.note: 'Do not alter this assessment' means the results leave intact the judgment that AI falls short of AGI. The draft's 'do not show general intelligence' is close to that. 'Isolated' is the part of the claim that can be checked as fact.

contract.note: The contract scores only the factual basis: whether the successes were few and at the easy or obscure end. The 'do not alter' judgment itself cannot be checked. That reading is flagged, and it is fair to the speaker's word 'isolated'.

evidence.note: January 2026 report quoting Tao: AI suits the obscure 'long tail', where many problems have straightforward solutions. This is within the period.
Tao's January 2026 tally: 8 cases of autonomous progress and 6 built on earlier literature, out of more than 1,000 problems. Humans were still needed. This fits 'isolated'.
Summary reviewed by Tao, available on the evaluation date: in January 2026 the success rate was 1-2%, concentrated at the easy end, with the median problem not yet in reach.
For early 2026, it says AI had made no real progress on marquee problems. The September 2026 gains fall outside the period and are context only.

reviews.rationale: Expert tallies from the period, mainly Tao's, show AI successes were a small share, concentrated at the easy or obscure end, and partly built on existing literature. The flagged counterevidence (e4) is about later progress outside the period. Only the factual basis is scored; the 'do not alter' judgment cannot be checked.

semantics.note: Revision 2 restores both the concession and the 'original concept of AGI' qualifier. It is an observation about systems current at the post.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: AI cannot handle unfamiliar settings or find its own goals without help. Including March 2026 evaluations of models current at the post is a flagged but reasonable choice.

evidence.note: ARC-AGI-3 in March 2026: frontier models current at the post scored under 1% in instruction-free novel environments, while humans scored 100%.
The benchmark maintainers describe what ARC-AGI-3 measures: exploration, acquiring goals, adaptation. This is background, not an outcome.
The February 2026 METR time-horizon result shows rising capability on well-specified tasks. It supports only the concession that systems are powerful and increasingly useful.
The February 2026 Nature comment argues human-level AI is already here. It is an argument, not a measurement, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: ARC-AGI-3 results from the period show frontier models near zero on self-directed, novel-environment tasks that humans solve. METR shows strong gains on narrower, well-specified tasks, which matches the concession. The opposing Nature piece is opinion and does not count against the claim.
